name: Feverfew
grown_as: A short-lived perennial herb that self-seeds freely, in William's herbs. The ordinary single white form is described; double and golden-leaved forms exist. ⚠️ CHECK which William has.
habit: A bushy, upright, branched clump 30 to 60 cm high, the stems ridged. The whole plant has a strong bitter smell when touched.

leaf.type: Simple but deeply cut (pinnately) into about 3 to 7 pairs of oblong lobes, each lobe itself cut into rounded teeth or smaller lobes
leaf.outline: Broadly oval to triangular overall, 4 to 10 cm
leaf.margin: Rounded teeth and small lobes on every lobe
leaf.veins: A clear midrib running into each lobe

flower.petals: About 10 to 20 short, broad white rays, square-ended with small teeth, no longer than the disc is wide
flower.centre: A large, flat, button-like yellow disc, 5 to 8 mm across
flower.behind: Hairy green bracts with narrow papery edges
flower.carried: Many together in loose, flat-topped clusters at the tops of the stems, facing up

fruit: Clusters of dry brown button heads. Seeds tiny, about 1.5 mm, pale brown and ribbed, with a short toothed crown at the top.
seedling: Two small round to oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are already lobed and yellow-green.
winter: Semi-evergreen: a low clump of lobed leaves at the base, the old flowering stems dead or cut away.

leaf: yellow-green leaf deeply cut into pairs of oblong lobes
every lobe itself with rounded teeth
bloom: small daisy with short broad white rays
rays no longer than the disc is wide
seed: tiny pale ribbed seed with a small crown
seedling: first true leaf lobed and yellow-green
young: compact bushy clump of yellow-green lobed leaves
flower: many small white daisies in flat-topped clusters
over a bushy yellow-green plant 30 to 60 cm
seedhead: dried brown button heads in clusters
dormant: low clump of lobed green leaves at the base
old stems dead or cut back

look_alikes: Scentless mayweed has thread-like leaves and larger single heads. Ox-eye daisy has much larger single heads and undivided leaves. Tansy has rayless yellow buttons and long, fern-like leaves. Corn chamomile is grey and downy with heads borne singly.
